sections.what_happened: [VERIFIED FACT -- the alert was issued] Saudi Arabia's Civil Defence issued a 'potential danger' alert for the Eastern Province cities of Dammam, Abqaiq and Dhahran and the al-Ahsa governorate at 01:57 GMT, via the national early-warning platform. Minutes later the danger was declared passed (for-ex.news, 01:56 UTC timestamp). [UNVERIFIED -- what triggered it] Neither the alert nor the all-clear named the threat, a launch, an interception or any impact. No Ansar Allah claim for a Dammam/Abqaiq strike in-window; no Saudi confirmation of any hit or damage. [CONTEXT -- why the east matters] Abqaiq is the world's largest oil-processing facility; the Nov 7 Saree six-operations claim (recorded 2100-01, sig 3, PASS) targeted Khurais, Riyadh and Dawadimi -- NOT Dammam/Abqaiq -- and its hits are unverified; the coalition DID intercept a Ansar Allah missile toward Riyadh province on Nov 7 (recorded 1600-01). Precedent pattern: brief eastern warnings followed by all-clears within minutes on Oct 13 (Dammam, after Ansar Allah threats vs Aramco HQ/Riyadh airport) and Jul 22 (Dammam; sirens in Bahrain). Oct 14: Ansar Allah DID strike Aramco HQ in Dhahran, damaging top floors (AP). Oct 21: Ansar Allah attack on King Fahd Airport, Dammam, killed 2 and injured 8 (Reuters). PortWatch backbone: NO new chokepoint count cited -- latest IMF PortWatch snapshot (portwatch-2026-11-08.json) is STALE (latest observation 2026-11-01, lag 7 days); Hormuz 7-day avg 4.43 transits vs 2025 baseline 85.53/day is a stale count and is NOT presented as live.
sections.what_verified: 1 tiered family for the alert itself: Al Jazeera (T2). The all-clear is carried only by for-ex.news (untiered -- not in the registry, attribution only). No second tiered family carries the warning at scan time.
sections.what_disputed: The alert named no threat and no strike followed it publicly; the all-clear within minutes matches the Oct 13 and Jul 22 false-alarm/precaution pattern. The Ansar Allah' Nov 7 claim named no Eastern Province target. Saudi Arabia has not confirmed any eastern strike or interception. The for-ex.news all-clear timestamp (01:56 UTC) precedes AJ's warning entry (01:57 GMT) by a minute -- sequencing within the minute is unresolved; treat as 'warning then all-clear minutes apart', not as a timed sequence.
sections.why_matters: Abqaiq on alert: Saudi Arabia just warned its oil heartland -- Dammam, Dhahran and Abqaiq, the plant that processes a huge share of the world's crude -- of 'potential danger', then called it off minutes later. What was incoming, and why won't anyone say?
sections.context: Background: IN-WINDOW (AJ liveblog entry 01:57 GMT = 05:57 ; for-ex.news 01:56 UTC) -- Saudi Civil Defence warns of 'potential danger' in the Eastern Province oil heartland (Dammam, Abqaiq, Dhahran, al-Ahsa), then calls it off minutes later; no strike confirmed, no threat named

totw_analysis: Our read: Abqaiq on alert: Saudi Arabia just warned its oil heartland -- Dammam, Dhahran and Abqaiq, the plant that processes a huge share of the world's crude -- of 'potential danger', then called it off minutes later. What was incoming, and why won't anyone say? The fault line our audience is arguing over: Did a Ansar Allah missile actually reach the Eastern Province, or is Riyadh hiding damage -- or are the Ansar Allah inventing hits that never happened?
